title: Range Addition
description: Brute force to optimized: touching every position in a range for every update versus a difference array that marks only the two endpoints, reconstructed with one prefix-sum sweep.

blocks.text: Problem Summary: Given an integer length and a list of update operations, each of the form [start, end, inc], build an array of size length, initialized to all zeros, and for each update, add inc to every element from index start to index end, inclusive. Return the final array after applying every update.

blocks.text: Starting from an all-zero array of the given length, apply every [start, end, inc] update by adding inc to each position from start to end, and return the resulting array once every update has been applied.

blocks.title: Analogy: Recording Deposits and Withdrawals Instead of Updating Every Day's Balance
blocks.text: Picture a bank balance that changes by a fixed amount over a range of days. Instead of walking through every day in the range and updating its balance individually, it is far faster to just note "add this amount starting on this day" and "undo it right after the range ends," then sweep through once at the very end to compute every day's actual balance.

blocks.caption: Mark the start and just-past-the-end; a running sum reconstructs every increment

blocks.text: Applying [1,3,2] adds 2 to indices 1-3; applying [2,4,3] adds 3 to indices 2-4; applying [0,2,-2] adds -2 to indices 0-2. The final array is [-2, 0, 3, 5, 3].
Before applying each update by walking through its entire range, notice that a range update can be represented by just two marks, at its start and just past its end.

blocks.title: Building the Intuition
blocks.text:
Observation 1: Adding inc to every position from start to end is the same as saying "the running total increases by inc starting at start, and decreases back by inc starting right after end."

Observation 2: Recording just those two marks, +inc at start and -inc at end plus 1, for every update, takes O(1) per update instead of O(range length).

Observation 3: After every update has been recorded as marks, a single left-to-right running sum over those marks reconstructs the exact final value at every position.

Observation 4: This is the classic difference array technique: represent range updates as point marks, then recover the actual array with one final prefix-sum pass.
This leads directly to marking only the two endpoints of each update in a difference array, then reconstructing the final array with a single prefix-sum sweep.
For every update, walk through its entire range directly, adding inc to each position.

items: Initialize an array of the given length to all zeros.
For every update [start, end, inc], add inc to every position from start to end.
Return the array after every update has been applied.

blocks.caption: Brute force flow: touch every position in a range, for every update

blocks.text: Why the code is written this way

items: Every update is applied fully and immediately, touching every position in its range one at a time.
The array is always in its fully up-to-date state after each update, at the cost of repeated work across overlapping ranges.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(length times updates.length) in the worst case, each update potentially touching the entire array.
Space: O(length) for the result array.

Limitation: touching every single position in a range is unnecessary work, since only the START and END of each update actually change the "rate" of accumulation, everything strictly between behaves identically until the next boundary.

blocks.title: The Optimization Journey
blocks.text:
Why touching every position is wasteful: a range update only changes behavior at exactly two points, where it starts, and right after where it ends; every position strictly inside the range experiences the exact same net effect.

What can represent that instead: a difference array, where diff[start] += inc records "the running total goes up by inc from here," and diff[end plus 1] -= inc records "and back down, right after the range ends."

How is the true array recovered: a single left-to-right running sum over the difference array reconstructs the exact value at every position, since the running sum naturally reflects however many active increments are "in effect" at that point.

The core idea: record each update as two O(1) marks in a difference array, then recover the final array with one prefix-sum pass at the very end.

For every update [start, end, inc], add inc to diff[start] and subtract inc from diff[end plus 1] in a difference array one longer than the result. Then sweep left to right, maintaining a running sum, and assign that running sum as the value at each position, in one single pass.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Update","Marks recorded"],"rows":[["[1,3,2]","diff[1] += 2, diff[4] -= 2"],["[2,4,3]","diff[2] += 3, diff[5] -= 3 (out of bounds, harmlessly ignored or sized for)"],["[0,2,-2]","diff[0] += -2, diff[3] -= -2"]]}

blocks.caption: Optimized flow: mark endpoints in O(1), reconstruct with one prefix-sum pass

codes.python:
def get_modified_array(length, updates):
    diff = [0] * (length + 1)
    for start, end, inc in updates:
        diff[start] += inc                 # increment begins here
        diff[end + 1] -= inc                # and is cancelled right after the range

    result = [0] * length
    running = 0
    for i in range(length):
        running += diff[i]                  # one sweep reconstructs the true value
        result[i] = running
    return result

blocks.text: Recording +inc at start and -inc at end plus 1 means that a running sum swept left to right will include inc at every position from start to end, and stop including it exactly at end plus 1, precisely matching what the range update was meant to do. Since this holds for every update independently, and their effects simply add together, one running sum over the combined difference array reconstructs the true final array in a single pass.

blocks.title: Time and Space Complexity
blocks.text:
Time: O(length plus updates.length), O(1) per update to record its marks, plus one linear sweep to build the result.
Space: O(length) for the difference array and result.

blocks.text: Range Addition is the textbook use case for the difference array technique: representing a range update with two O(1) marks, then recovering every actual value with a single final prefix-sum sweep, instead of touching every position for every update.

items: Forgetting to place the cancelling mark at end PLUS ONE, not at end itself, which would cut the range one position short.
Sizing the difference array too small to hold the end-plus-one mark when end is the last valid index.
Applying updates directly to the result array instead of recording them as marks first.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Case","Expected Behavior"],"rows":[["No updates at all","The result is all zeros."],["Overlapping updates on the same range","Their effects simply add together in the running sum."]]}

blocks.text: Explaining the difference array as "the running total changes rate exactly at a range's boundaries" is the clearest way to justify why only two marks per update are needed.

blocks.title: If The Interviewer Says This, Think This
blocks.text: If the interviewer says "can you avoid touching every position in a range", think: a difference array, marking only where an update starts and where it ends.

items: How would you support QUERYING an individual position's value between updates, without recomputing the whole array?

Any "apply many range updates, read the final array once" problem, the difference array's natural use case.

blocks.title: Complexity Summary
blocks.text: The brute force runs in O(length times updates.length) time; the optimized difference array approach runs in O(length plus updates.length) time. Both use O(length) space.

items: Pattern: the difference array technique, marking range update boundaries in O(1) and reconstructing the final array with one prefix-sum sweep.
Core Idea: a range update only changes behavior at its two boundaries; marking +inc at the start and -inc just after the end lets a single running sum reproduce every individual value.
Time: O(length times updates.length) for the brute force, O(length plus updates.length) for the optimized approach.
Most Important Observation: range updates only need to be recorded at their boundaries; everything in between is reconstructed automatically by a running sum.
Interview Difficulty: the difference array technique is simple once seen, and reused across many range-update problems.
One line memory trick: mark the start and just-past-the-end, then one prefix sum sweep rebuilds everything.
